season_garden_06_001.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_001.text: Heat arrived before the sixth garden afternoon had properly begun. Yue found the kitchen door propped in its permitted position, a damp cloth drying over a rail and the blue bird nearly white in the strong light beyond the shade. She had slept enough and eaten before coming, yet the short walk from the street left her thirsty. She filled her own cup from the staff-set drinking supply and sat until her breathing settled. The session would begin at its agreed time, not at the first moment she felt observed.

season_garden_06_002.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_002.text: Qiu arrived with dust on one boot and an irritated account of a cart blocking the ordinary crossing. She had chosen the longer permitted route rather than climb past it. “I am trying to stop treating a delay as a dare,” she said while washing her hands. Yue asked whether the extra walk changed her comfortable work limit for the afternoon. Qiu checked herself before saying no by habit. She asked for a seated first task and the same scheduled break they had already agreed.

season_garden_06_003.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_003.text: The selected planting stock had arrived through the gardener's actual authorized purchase. The treasurer held its receipt separately from the helpers' wages. Whether Yue had chosen seasonal annuals or one young plum, only that selected viable option had been bought and accepted. The unchosen possibility had not become a second project through private enthusiasm. Staff had checked the material on arrival and would direct the specific planting sequence. Yue saw that the safe bed was still smaller than the future she had imagined from the street.

season_garden_06_004.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_004.text: Today's first work followed that actual selection. Qiu laid her gauge on the light table without opening it, waiting to hear where measurement would help. Yue asked the gardener to place the permitted preparation within her comfortable reach. The kitchen woman stopped sweeping to look, then returned to the floor after receiving the actual brief update she wanted. Her expectation did not make the work public theater. The gardener drew the first task in chalk on the table's loose board, and the women began.

season_garden_06_005.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_005.text: By the first break, the selected planting had reached its actual staff-directed state and its future checks had been assigned. Yue's light work had stayed within the stated comfortable movements. Qiu had moved quickly on one small preparation and slowly on another, finding the material indifferent to her preferred reputation. The bed looked changed and not yet established. They returned their tools to the agreed shelf and washed their hands. The drinking supply was still available under staff's actual afternoon plan, and both women used it before arguing about anything.

season_garden_06_006.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_06_006.text: “It is difficult not to praise a planted thing as if it has already survived,” Qiu said. Yue looked toward the bed and agreed. The word begun felt smaller than the thing their hope wanted. Qiu said she liked it anyway because a beginning had an actual place to stand. Yue thought of the old tree ground beyond the closure. There was still no finished restoration there. A different safe bed had received the selected new work, and the garden did not have to hide the distinction to be alive.

season_garden_06_007.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_007.text: The pinwheel child's grandmother did not come outside that afternoon. Staff assessed and cared for her within the clinical team, and the family received the information they were authorized to have. The garden helpers were told only that the doorway should stay quiet and that no visit to the court was planned. Yue thought of the requested yellow flowers or the young buds she might have enjoyed, then returned to the light table. The planting's usefulness would not be judged by whether one person's care happened to permit a viewing today.

season_garden_06_008.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_008.text: The child's accompanying adult arrived without him and carried a small cloth parcel for the room. She looked tired enough that Yue began to offer a chair, then asked which one would be useful. The woman chose the backed chair near the dining hall and sat before taking the parcel in. She wanted three quiet minutes more than an account of the garden. Qiu moved the nearby tray so nobody had to turn sideways past her. The small change let the woman's pause remain unremarkable.

season_garden_06_009.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_06_009.text: “Would you like water?” Yue asked. The woman said yes and pointed to the ordinary drinking cup she preferred. Yue brought it from the permitted supply and asked where to put it. The woman drank slowly, then said she had been talking all morning and did not want to explain another thing. Yue answered that she could rest without explaining to the helpers. Qiu went back to the label table. Their attention became useful partly by ending before it demanded another sentence from the person it wanted to care for.

season_garden_06_010.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_010.text: The family member entered the room with staff permission after the brief rest. From the table, Yue could hear neither private conversation nor clinical findings. She could see the parcel's empty wrapping later returned to the woman's bag. A visit had happened; what it contained remained the family's own. Qiu asked Yue if it was hard not knowing. Yue said it was, particularly when uncertainty gave her so much room to fear. Qiu answered that fear was a poor reason to claim somebody else's story. Both remained afraid.

season_garden_06_011.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_011.text: The afternoon's shared light assignment was to prepare a small clear notice for garden users describing the safe route, current shelter limits and who owned planting questions. Staff supplied the actual wording. Yue copied it in large readable letters and Qiu checked the route arrows against the permitted approach. They did not add clinical advice or declare the new planting a treatment. The work needed to be understood by someone arriving tired, distracted or unfamiliar with the site, not admired by another practitioner who already knew where everything belonged.

season_garden_06_012.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_012.text: Qiu placed the draft where a visitor would first see it and found the blue bird drawing on an unrelated sample board more eye-catching than the route arrow. She moved the draft within the permitted notice space after staff approved the position. Yue watched from the approach and described which line reached her attention first. Their review used actual arrival rather than standing proudly beside the paper. The final notice remained an ordinary sign. It could help someone find the route without making every future mistake impossible.

season_garden_06_013.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_013.text: A man leaving the apothecary stopped near the dining hall and put one hand against the wall. He said he needed a moment, then bent forward with an expression that made Qiu call the responsible staff immediately. Yue kept the nearby light trays out of the passage and followed the staff member's request to bring an available chair. Neither woman tried to name the cause or treat him with qi. The scene moved quickly because the staff had a clear role, and the helpers could answer specific small instructions.

season_garden_06_014.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_014.text: Ren Qiao and the trained staff took clinical responsibility, moving the man to the appropriate care space while preserving privacy and managing the route. Yue heard only what the helpers needed for their own task: keep this turn clear, bring no more visitors here, return the light table's work when safe. Qiu stood with her empty cup in her hand until she realized she was holding it too tightly. The man had become ill in a real place with people responsible for helping him. The garden did not require the practitioners to become his miraculous rescuers.

season_garden_06_015.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_015.text: After staff released the route, Yue returned the unused chair according to their instruction. Her shoulder had tolerated the light requested movement, yet the sudden rush left her trembling with remembered fear. She sat rather than interpret the tremor as a demand to do more. Qiu asked whether she wanted company or space. Yue chose company without more questions for a few minutes. Qiu took the neighboring chair. Their silence held the fact that something frightening had happened and the fact that their own work had a smaller part within it.

season_garden_06_016.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_06_016.text: “I knew to call quickly,” Qiu said when Yue was ready to hear her. “Then I wanted another thing to do because waiting felt like failing him.” Yue said moving the trays and bringing the requested chair had given her hands a safe purpose; afterward she had felt the same emptiness. They did not know the private result and would not demand it to make their own reaction settle. Staff would tell authorized people what they needed to know. The two helpers could still speak about the part that belonged to their own experience.

season_garden_06_017.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_017.text: Yue thanked Qiu for noticing the man and calling staff promptly. Qiu thanked Yue for clearing the turn without needing another instruction while staff approached. Their different habits had helped at different moments. Neither wanted the incident entered as a contest between speed and care. The man had been ill, and trained people had taken responsibility. The helpers had carried out limited useful actions. They could acknowledge each other without making someone else's distress the evidence that finally proved one method or one person superior.

season_garden_06_018.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_018.text: The kitchen woman brought their next permitted light task: sorting washed cloth ties that staff had already identified as suitable for future minor maintenance. The simple work gave Yue's hands something quieter to do. Qiu began counting too fast, stopped when she lost the sequence and started again at the last confirmed stack. Yue said she did not have to make her body obey the count before she had settled. Qiu answered that counting helped her settle if she did not turn it into a race. They let the slower rhythm be chosen, not imposed.

season_garden_06_019.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_019.text: A kitchen worker told them the public turn could be used normally again under the staff's current notice. She offered no private clinical outcome. Yue thanked her for the site update. The man had an authorized care team and people who could receive his actual news; the helpers' wish to know did not add them to that circle. Qiu looked at the notice they had been preparing and said its clear route arrow suddenly felt less dull. Yue agreed. Ordinary access work could matter most when nobody had time to admire it.

season_garden_06_020.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_020.text: The gardener came to check the selected planting after its initial staff-directed work. He described the actual surface condition and assigned the next ordinary observation under the accepted maintenance plan. Nothing in the hot afternoon proved establishment or failure yet. Qiu asked what a helper should report if a visible change appeared during a permitted session. The gardener named concrete observations and the staff contact, not a diagnosis. Yue wrote the useful instruction beside the light task list and kept her larger anxious predictions off the stock record.

season_garden_06_021.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_06_021.text: “When I am afraid, I want every leaf to tell me whether the future will be kind,” Yue said. Qiu answered that she wanted the gauge to do the same. The gardener, overhearing, said leaves mostly told him about particular present conditions if he looked carefully enough and knew what he was comparing. He returned to his actual check. Yue laughed quietly. The world could provide information without answering the emotional question she had hidden inside the request. Her fear might need company even when the plant needed water.

season_garden_06_022.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_022.text: The bench owner came to sit for a while after finishing the greens. She asked whether the helpers had enjoyed seeing the actual planting work begin. Qiu said yes and admitted the quietness afterward had surprised her. The owner said new work often looked least impressive immediately after it was done. The old tree had once been a stick her husband was certain would die. He had complained about it until it was large enough to shade his chair. She smiled, then said she was probably remembering only the complaints she liked.

season_garden_06_023.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_023.text: Yue asked if the woman wanted that planting memory included in the garden's ordinary history notes. She said not today. She had told it because she felt like talking on her bench. Yue thanked her and left it off the work sheet. A offered story could become useful company without being collected for public heritage. Qiu sat on the available chair and asked what the husband had complained about when the tree finally shaded him. The woman said he complained that the birds had discovered his chair before he had.

season_garden_06_024.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_024.text: That made Qiu laugh loudly enough to look toward the quiet room afterward. Staff had kept the doorway closed for privacy and rest, and the ordinary permitted conversation in the court remained acceptable at its current level. She lowered her voice without treating her laughter as a moral failure. Yue was glad that care did not require every living person in the garden to become solemn all afternoon. The bench owner could remember a funny husband while another family had a difficult visit, and neither feeling erased the other.

season_garden_06_025.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_025.text: The man who had been taken into care was not brought back to give the helpers a grateful final scene. Staff retained the actual clinical process and the authorized communication. Yue let the work session continue with the small unfinished feeling that reality often left. Qiu admitted she might think about him later. Yue said she might too. They could seek their own ordinary support if the fright lingered, without asking his private outcome to perform that support for them. The cloth stacks grew in a quiet counted row.

season_garden_06_026.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_026.text: Su checked whether the incident had changed either helper's remaining comfortable work limit. Yue wanted the last table assignment seated, with no extra carrying. Qiu wanted a brief pause before continuing the count. They agreed the revised order with the responsible worker; actual completed time would still be paid under the existing partial-time rule if either needed to finish early. Neither had to stage collapse to make a smaller change legitimate. Both chose to complete the safe remaining light work after their breaks, and the work stayed limited to the original session.

season_garden_06_027.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_027.text: The child arrived late with his accompanying adult, who had already arranged the present visit through staff. He asked whether the boat mast could be painted blue like the bird. His adult said they could discuss paint at home and did not borrow the garden's materials to avoid disappointing him. Yue asked what sort of hull he had chosen. He described a piece of clean household scrap his adult had approved. Qiu asked if the boat needed to float or only sail on a shelf. He said both, then reconsidered the shelf.

season_garden_06_028.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_028.text: Yue enjoyed the child's willingness to change the purpose before defending a design. Qiu said his boat would be more sensible than several apparatus proposals she had seen. The adult laughed and asked him whether he wanted to show the drawing to his grandmother during the brief permitted visit. He did. The family went inside. The helpers returned to their label check without waiting to be told whether the conversation was happy. A chosen family visit could remain meaningful beyond what the garden workers were allowed to see.

season_garden_06_029.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_029.text: The new route notice received staff's final approval and was placed in the agreed visible position. Yue checked it from the ordinary approach once more. Qiu checked that its edge did not protrude into the passing line or obscure the actual closure warning. The blue bird remained on the bench, where it had a different audience and purpose. Nobody asked the sign to be beautiful enough to console grief. It needed to be readable, current and owned by someone who would update it when the actual site conditions changed.

season_garden_06_030.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_030.text: The gardener set the next check for the selected planting under his accepted ordinary plan and told them what light preparation the seventh session might contain if conditions held. Yue asked about the forthcoming hot interval and the actual water supply. He described its present bounded allocation and the staff's adjustment process if the conditions changed. Qiu did not promise to bring water privately from her home. The plan needed a sustainable actual source, not a helper's temporary heroic effort hiding that the agreed arrangement had stopped fitting the weather.

season_garden_06_031.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_031.text: At closing, Su recorded the sixth completed three-hour session for each woman and paid three copper each, bringing their garden wages to eighteen copper apiece. The selected planting's actual purchase cost now appeared in its own materials account, alongside the completed bench repair. Only the actual selected option had been spent. Su read that specific balance from the accepted receipt and retained the unspent reserve for real future work. Yue checked her own wage, then closed the purse. The hot afternoon's care and fear could not be reduced to its arithmetic.

season_garden_06_032.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_06_032.text: “Today I was useful because I was quick,” Qiu said at the gate, “and because I stopped when the staff had the work.” Yue answered that both mattered. Qiu looked up at the clear gap where the damaged crown had been. “I do not want us to make a clever lesson out of that man,” she added. Yue agreed. Their own actions could be discussed; his distress could remain his. The new planting was elsewhere in the garden, begun under its selected plan, and would need a different kind of attention tomorrow.

season_garden_06_033.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_033.text: Yue took a drink before starting home and followed the ordinary street in the shade where it was available. Her shoulder was tired, and her mind kept returning to the sudden hand against the wall. She did not punish herself for the memory. She had acted within the useful part she could own and left treatment to the people qualified for it. At home she would eat, rest and decide whether she wanted to speak with someone she actually trusted. The garden's unfinished questions could wait outside that supper.

season_garden_06_purchase_gate.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_purchase_gate.text: The treasurer named the actual selected purchase before the helpers' preparation began. Seasonal annual stock had a three-copper receipt; suitable young plum stock and its materials had an eight-copper receipt. Only the one selected by Yue's actual planting decision belonged to this afternoon. The gardener had accepted its arrival and would direct the corresponding work. Qiu waited for that instruction rather than opening the gauge as a promise. Yue moved her supported tray close enough that her first useful action would not cost an unnecessary reach.

season_garden_06_annuals_01.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_annuals_01.text: The seasonal annuals were the selected purchase. Staff had received the approved yellow marigold seed and light planting materials for the authorized three copper, paid from the garden materials allowance. With the earlier six-copper bench repair, nine copper had now actually been spent on materials and thirty-one remained in that allowance. The gardener checked the packet against the agreed stock and plan before any seed left it. Yue saw a small ordinary envelope, much less brilliant than the bed Qiu had imagined indoors.

season_garden_06_annuals_02.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_annuals_02.text: The gardener divided the actual selected seed count into twenty-four seeds for this first modest sowing and eight retained under suitable storage for possible staff-authorized resowing. The packet held no unlimited future supply. Yue copied those counts onto the approved stock label and left the sowing date blank until the action happened. Qiu sorted the light containers by the gardener's chosen use. She asked if sowing all thirty-two would be more likely to give somebody flowers. He answered with the real bed width and water plan rather than a promise about abundance.

season_garden_06_annuals_03.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_06_annuals_03.text: “I want the extra eight to count as hope,” Qiu said. The gardener said they could count as a limited practical option for particular failed emergence, after actual observation. Hope could accompany that option without changing its quantity. Yue wrote retained eight and then stopped, smiling at how stern the small line looked beside their conversation. Qiu said she preferred its sternness to a cupboard that somehow supplied another packet whenever somebody hoped for a brighter result. The seeds remained actual stock, not an argument.

season_garden_06_annuals_04.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_annuals_04.text: Staff prepared the bed's soil after its safe drainage and permitted condition were checked. Yue and Qiu did not do the heavier digging. The gardener showed the intended sowing positions on a light tray so the helpers could prepare readable markers and suitable small covers at the table. Yue kept her shoulder supported while handling those light pieces. Qiu checked the count against the real tray and caught one duplicated marker. She laughed at herself, corrected it and showed Yue where the mistake had come from before the sowing began.

season_garden_06_annuals_05.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_annuals_05.text: The twenty-four seeds looked different when they were actually laid out. Some were shorter, one carried a pale husk, and none resembled a flower. Qiu asked whether the pale one should be excluded. The gardener assessed it using his own stock knowledge and actual comparison, retaining or replacing it within the agreed count as appropriate. The helpers followed that decision. They did not invent a new sorting rule from what looked attractive. Yue admired how a small trained action could protect a future without pretending to know exactly what would emerge.

season_garden_06_annuals_06.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_annuals_06.text: The gardener directed the sowing depth and spacing, doing the ground work that belonged to his role. The helpers carried out only the specific light permitted task he assigned, one small controlled movement at a time within their comfortable limits. Yue prepared markers at the table and Qiu passed the counted light pieces from the designated safe position. Neither pushed through resistance to prove dedication. The bed's visible change was slight: small prepared lines, fresh labels and soil handled according to its actual present condition.

season_garden_06_annuals_07.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_06_annuals_07.text: “I expected planting to feel like announcing something,” Yue said. Qiu said she had expected a little more color at the beginning of a flower plan. The gardener chuckled and completed the ordinary sowing record with its actual date. He said the bed's first useful appearance was the one that told staff what had been done and how to care for it. Yue placed the readable label where he directed, and the future flowers remained future. A seed could begin without performing reassurance for the people who had chosen it.

season_garden_06_annuals_08.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_annuals_08.text: The approved light cover protected the initial bed under the gardener's suitable ordinary plan. Its edges stayed inside the permitted planting area, clear of the route and the resting ledge. Qiu checked the visible fastening positions against his marked instructions. Yue counted the accepted spare ties and returned unused ones to their actual stock. Nothing trapped or harmed visiting birds. The sparrow from the shelter landed nearby, inspected the new arrangement and flew toward another ordinary appetite. The garden's future did not require making it the enemy of the afternoon.

season_garden_06_annuals_09.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_annuals_09.text: The gardener watered according to the observed soil and the accepted bounded garden supply. He showed where the ordinary daily allocation was kept and who would check whether a later adjustment was needed. The helpers could report the assigned visible conditions during their permitted sessions; they did not take over the staff rota or promise to bring endless water from home. Qiu watched the small darker patch spread through the soil. “It looks as if something has already happened,” she said. Yue answered that sowing and watering really had happened.

season_garden_06_annuals_10.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_annuals_10.text: That distinction pleased Qiu more than she expected. She could name a completed action without naming flowers. Yue could respect the care without making every delay a virtue. They stood outside the planting boundary while the gardener finished his record and secured the retained eight seeds in proper storage. The safe bed had become an actual sown bed under staff care. It had not become an established flowering patch, and both women could still want that future. The desire had a real beginning to wait beside now.

season_garden_06_annuals_11.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_annuals_11.text: The bench owner asked to see the label after the gardener permitted an ordinary look from the safe route. She said the large letters were easier than the old small labels. Yue told her Qiu had supplied the useful guide earlier. Qiu asked whether the date was clear too. The woman nodded, then said she cared more about the yellow. They laughed. A readable label could support actual care while the person watching from a bench continued to want beauty rather than an explanation of inventory.

season_garden_06_annuals_12.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_annuals_12.text: The owner's adult son asked whether the flower bed would need more land later if every seed emerged. The gardener explained the actual thinning and maintenance plan for that modest sowing, with any selected surplus managed through his ordinary responsible work. No extra bed had been accepted. The son looked at the small rectangle and said he liked that it did not take the bench's clear approach. Yue watched his mother shift comfortably on the sound seat. The planting choice had honored a present arrangement already useful to someone.

season_garden_06_annuals_13.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_06_annuals_13.text: Qiu asked whether the grandmother wanted a brief ordinary update that sowing had actually happened. Staff returned her present preference through the person attending her: she wanted to hear when something was visible above the soil, rather than every step before it. Qiu accepted that without disappointment becoming another request. The earlier wish for yellow flowers did not make the patient available for unlimited progress reports. Yue liked the specificity. The garden could care for the seeds today and leave the patient the quiet update she had chosen.

season_garden_06_annuals_14.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_annuals_14.text: The child arrived later with his visiting adult and looked at the covered bed from the permitted route. He asked if the cover was a blanket for flowers. The gardener explained its actual use in simple terms and said the seeds were still below the soil. The child thought their work looked sleepy. Yue said sleep was not the gardener's word for it, but waiting for growth could be quiet. Qiu asked whether the boat mast at home needed something done today. He said it needed a person to stop touching the glue.

season_garden_06_annuals_15.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_annuals_15.text: That gave Yue and Qiu an unexpectedly useful image without a borrowed biological claim. They laughed at the household instruction and let it remain about the boat's actual glue. The seed bed had its own care needs, which staff would follow rather than copy from the child's craft. His adult told him it was time for the arranged visit. He went inside with the drawing. The newly sown flowers did not need to become a lesson that every passing person carried away. They could remain plants entrusted to ordinary care.

season_garden_06_annuals_16.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_annuals_16.text: Before the break, the gardener inspected the label placement, light cover and immediate route clearance. He accepted the helpers' completed preparation and retained responsibility for the actual next checks. Yue returned the spare markers to their stock. Qiu counted the eight retained seeds on the sealed record without opening their packet again. The orderly ending satisfied her need for a completed handover. It left uncertainty exactly where it belonged: future emergence and survival under changing ordinary conditions, rather than whether the actual sowing had happened at all.

season_garden_06_annuals_17.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_06_annuals_17.text: “I am glad we chose them,” Yue said. “I am still sorry about the tree we didn't choose.” Qiu answered that she was relieved the second sentence did not mean Yue wanted to reverse the plan in secret. They stood beside the safe bed and let the unchosen wish remain a wish. An actual commitment needed steadiness while conditions held, and could still be reviewed when facts changed. The gardener had accepted this modest sowing. The helpers did not have to be emotionally unanimous to perform their part carefully.

season_garden_06_annuals_18.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_annuals_18.text: The treasurer's material record now held the actual three-copper receipt, leaving thirty-one copper in the materials allowance after the earlier bench payment. The unused future tree cost was absent because no tree had been bought. The selected seeds, their actual sowing and the staff-owned next care were recorded; the retained eight remained in identified stock. Yue and Qiu washed their hands for the shared rest break with one real planting begun. The first new leaves would need their own actual observation before anyone could report them to the patient waiting indoors.

season_garden_06_plum_01.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_plum_01.text: The young plum was the selected purchase. Staff had received suitable inspected stock and its required planting materials for the authorized eight copper, paid from the garden materials allowance. With the earlier six-copper bench repair, fourteen copper had now actually been spent on materials and twenty-six remained in that allowance. The gardener checked the tree against the accepted plan before moving it into the safe bed. Yue saw a slender ordinary living thing, much smaller than the shade her imagination had tried to borrow.

season_garden_06_plum_02.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_plum_02.text: Qiu crouched outside the handling area and studied the buds. They were not tiny sails after all, at least to her eyes. The child's question could wait for his own view. The gardener showed the present root and stem condition relevant to receiving the stock, retaining the assessment within his professional role. The helpers did not diagnose the tree by running qi along it or treat a brown mark as an omen. Yue liked its modest size and felt a pang at how much care a small future could require.

season_garden_06_plum_03.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
season_garden_06_plum_03.text: “I can see why you wanted it,” Qiu said. “I still wanted flowers.” Yue answered that both sentences belonged here. The selected tree had been bought under an actual modest care plan; the annual packet had not. Qiu asked where her gauge would help without intruding into the gardener's planting judgment. He pointed to a limited marked support measurement for the light preparation. She made that measurement at the table, checked it against his instruction and wrote it clearly enough that somebody else could follow it after she left.

season_garden_06_plum_04.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_plum_04.text: Staff prepared the heavier hole and handled the tree within their trained planting sequence. Yue and Qiu kept clear of the work line and helped only with the assigned light ties, markers and permitted surface protection. Yue's table stayed supported at a comfortable reach. Qiu sorted the approved ties by the gardener's actual plan rather than improvising a firmer arrangement because it looked more secure. A support too tight could create its own harm. The gardener explained the appropriate slack and retained final fitting responsibility himself.

season_garden_06_plum_05.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_plum_05.text: The tree entered the prepared ground at the gardener's directed depth and orientation. Staff settled the soil and fitted the ordinary supports according to the inspected plan. No personal Four-pair circuit bore the tree, moved the ground or promised its roots instant strength. Yue watched the unremarkable work and felt gratitude for its lack of spectacle. She did not need the planting to look as though one difficult hour could restore a mature crown. It could be a trained team placing one young tree where its accepted future care could actually reach it.

season_garden_06_plum_06.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_06_plum_06.text: “I expected to feel certain once it was in the ground,” Yue said. Qiu answered that she had expected the actual thing to argue more persuasively against the flowers. The gardener laughed quietly and checked the final support. He said planting made a present responsibility clearer; it did not make survival guaranteed. Yue understood that as an action she could name. The tree had arrived and been planted under its actual care plan. Its establishment would remain a future observation, with the staff owning the relevant checks.

season_garden_06_plum_07.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_plum_07.text: The approved surface protection stayed within the safe bed and left the route's clear turn unchanged. Qiu passed the counted light pieces where directed and returned unused materials to their actual stock. Yue prepared the readable label with the real planting date after the gardener confirmed it. The new tree was not named as a memorial or a replacement for a particular person. Its ordinary stock identifier and care information served the people responsible for maintaining it. Others could give it their own private associations without rewriting that practical beginning.

season_garden_06_plum_08.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_plum_08.text: The gardener watered according to the current soil condition and accepted bounded supply, then showed staff where the next ordinary check sat in their rota. Yue and Qiu would not silently acquire watering duties between sessions or after their ten-week agreement ended. The garden had accepted that actual responsibility through its existing staff plan. Qiu asked what visible change a helper should report during permitted work. The gardener named the limited useful observations and the appropriate contact. The question gave her attentiveness somewhere real to go.

season_garden_06_plum_09.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_plum_09.text: The tree looked slightly crooked from the bench. The owner asked whether it had been planted wrong. The gardener checked the actual fit and explained the sound intended alignment against the natural shape of the young stem. A pleasing line from one seat was not the same as a suitable planting. The woman accepted the explanation and said she would probably keep seeing the lean. Qiu smiled. A good result could leave somebody with an ordinary visual complaint that did not prove the responsible work had failed.

season_garden_06_plum_10.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_plum_10.text: The owner's son came to look during the permitted viewing interval and said he remembered his father's impatience with another small tree. His mother answered that this one should be spared the family tradition of predictions that it would die. He laughed and corrected himself: he hoped it would establish well under its actual care. Yue appreciated the changed sentence without making it a ritual everyone had to repeat. The new plum had begun beside real lives with awkward habits, and those habits could change without being perfectly remade in one afternoon.

season_garden_06_plum_11.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_plum_11.text: Qiu asked whether the grandmother wanted a brief ordinary update that the selected tree had actually been planted. Staff returned her present preference through the person attending her: she wanted to hear about visible buds opening when that happened, rather than every preparation step. Qiu accepted the answer without turning it into a request to enjoy the tree sooner. The earlier flower wish remained acknowledged, and the new plant did not claim to compensate fully for it. Yue liked that the patient could choose the timing and size of her own attention.

season_garden_06_plum_12.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_plum_12.text: The child arrived later with his accompanying adult and saw the tree from the permitted route. He said the buds looked like tightly closed little fists. Qiu admitted that he had found a better shape than her imagined sails. He asked whether he could touch one. The gardener's present protection rules kept the young tree undisturbed, and the adult helped him follow that limit. Yue suggested he could draw what he saw if he wanted. He chose to look instead, saving the paper for the boat at home.

season_garden_06_plum_13.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_plum_13.text: The child circled only within the allowed viewing place and decided the tree was not very exciting yet. His adult said it did not need to entertain him. Qiu laughed at how much she sympathized with the complaint. Yue told him she liked seeing a small thing begin even when she could not yet point to its best future use. He said that sounded like glue drying. They let the comparison remain a joke about his actual boat. The gardener's care plan would not be replaced by a child's craft instructions.

season_garden_06_plum_14.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_plum_14.text: A sparrow landed near the young plum and pecked at a dry husk outside the protected planting. The owner asked whether birds would damage its buds. The gardener described the present ordinary checks and suitable nonharmful protection within the actual accepted plan, without promising that no living thing would ever touch the tree. Qiu watched the bird leave. She said a planted future had more neighbors than a fixture on a workbench. Yue answered that the bench also had neighbors; they were merely easier to overlook when concentrating on the dial.

season_garden_06_plum_15.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_plum_15.text: Before the break, the gardener checked the support, label, watering and immediate route clearance. He accepted the helpers' light preparation and retained final responsibility for the actual planting and establishment checks. Qiu wrote the limited gauge measurement beside the staff's marked support plan, giving her quick careful work a clear owner and purpose. Yue returned the spare labels. The tree did not look much changed after the final check. A safe handover could be almost invisible to someone watching from the doorway and still be important.

season_garden_06_plum_16.speaker: lin_yue
season_garden_06_plum_16.text: “I am glad we chose it,” Yue said. “I am still sorry we didn't choose the flowers.” Qiu answered that she would probably say the reverse if the annuals had won. The admission made them both smile. The unchosen use could stay worthy without becoming an unpaid second project hidden in their bags. The gardener had accepted one modest young plum under the staff's real care. The helpers would carry out their assigned part and let their mixed feelings remain smaller than the living thing's need for a steady actual plan.

season_garden_06_plum_17.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_plum_17.text: The treasurer's materials record now held the actual eight-copper receipt, leaving twenty-six copper in the materials allowance after the earlier bench payment. No annual seed cost appeared because no annual bed had been bought. The young stock, its actual planting and the staff-owned next care were recorded. The former old-tree ground remained under its own closure until qualified checks allowed change. Yue looked between that gap and the new safe bed, allowing a beginning to exist without telling either place that the other had been restored.

season_garden_06_plum_18.speaker: narrator
season_garden_06_plum_18.text: They washed their hands and returned to the shared rest break. Qiu put her gauge back in its own cord and Yue sat with her shoulder supported. The actual planted plum remained outside under its ordinary accepted care, a small shape that could not yet shade anyone. The grandmother's chosen update would wait for a real visible change. Both practitioners kept their present Four-pair qualification and their remaining finite garden sessions. A new tree had enlarged the place's future possibilities without enlarging their power or purchasing the lives beyond their agreed afternoons.
